topic: Two-wheeler riders: dust, wind and insects — visor/glasses, don't rub

youtube.title: Dust in your eye on the bike? Don't rub! 🏍️ #Shorts
youtube.description:
Dust in your eye while riding? Don't rub. Do this instead.
பைக்கில் கண்ணில் தூசு? தேய்க்காதீர்கள்!

• The cornea (clear front of the eye) is delicate; rubbing drags grit across it and can scratch it.
• Pull over safely, blink a few times and rinse with clean water; tears often wash it out.
• Ride with a clear helmet visor down, or wear wraparound glasses (power glasses help too).
• Wind dries the eyes fast, which is why they water and sting on long rides.
• Don't dig it out with a finger, cloth corner or anything sharp.
• Urgent: pain, blurred vision, still feels stuck after rinsing, or anything that hit the eye at speed.
• Clear vision keeps you safe on the road: get your eyes tested.

gmb.text:
Two-wheeler riders: protect your eyes from dust, wind and insects. If something gets in your eye, don't rub: rubbing can scratch the clear front of the eye. Pull over safely, blink a few times and rinse with clean water.

Keep a clear helmet visor down or wear wraparound glasses on every ride. Never try to dig anything out with a finger, a cloth corner or anything sharp.

See an eye specialist urgently if there is pain, blurred vision, it still feels stuck after rinsing, or something hit your eye at speed. Clear vision keeps you safe on the road. Book an eye test on WhatsApp: 044 4356 9998
